raw_case_text:
A 78-year old male patient with RA treated with tofacitinib (10 mg p.o. daily), methotrexate (20 mg p.o. weekly) and low dose corticosteroids (prednisolone 5 mg p.o. daily), was admitted to hospital with a 2-week history of arthralgia, nausea and confusion (Additional file 1). RA was diagnosed 6 months ago, as the patient fulfilled the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria with bilateral symmetric swollen and tender joints (wrists, hands and feet; over 10 affected joints in total) and arthralgia for 3 years (negative anti-CCP antibody and negative rheumatoid factor IgM). No signs of erosions were found on X-ray (hands and feet). Therapy was initiated with prednisone (20 mg/day) and MTX 15 mg/week s.c. with increasing doses over time. Tofacitinib was initiated 2 months prior hospital admission due to lack of efficacy of MTX monotherapy (MTX was switched to p.o. at that time, as the patient disliked injections).
At time of admission the patient reported shortness of breath on exertion but not at rest.
Physical examination showed following vital signs: temperature (auricular): 36.5  C blood pressure: 178/95 mmHg, heart rate: 75 bpm, oxygen saturation: 88-90% at rest and on exercise 80% on room air. Wrists and ankles were swollen and tender bilaterally symmetric. There were normal findings on auscultation of heart and lungs without any other signs of venous congestion.
Laboratory findings on admission revealed hypercalcemia (albumin-corrected 3.12 mmol/l (normal range 2.0-2.6 mmol/l) and elevated 1,25- dihydroxyvitamin D levels (162 ng/l, normal range 22-111 ng/l). PTH was appropriately low at < 0.5 pmol/l (normal range < 1.3 pmol/l). Further laboratory findings are described in Table 1.
Further investigation of hypercalcemia included a whole body CT scan, which showed bilateral interstitial pneumonic infiltrates without pleural effusions (Fig. 1). The patient was referred from normal ward care to the ICU due to acute respiratory failure requiring non-invasive ventilation/ high-flow oxygen therapy. PCR from bronchoalveloar lavage (BAL) was positive for P. jirovecii and Rhinovirus A/B/C and a diagnosis of PJP was made with colonization of Rhinovirus. Adequate therapy with TMP/SMX i.v. (15 mg/kg/d) and prednisolone p.o. (1 mg/kg/d) was initiated. Treatment with TMP/SMX was stopped after 10 days because of severe hyponatremia (drop from 136 mmol/l to 119 mmol/l; normal range 136-144 mmol/l) and acutely worsening confusion, which was attributed most likely to acute hyponatremia or as a direct adverse drug reaction to TMP/SMX. As second line therapy we initiated clindamycin and primaquine. Confusion improved but thrombocytopenia developed (drop from 441 G/l to 83 G/l) 4 days later, which was felt to be due to primaquine and led to the discontinuation of clindamycin and primaquine.
Both the patient's clinical condition and hypercalcemia were improved after 17 days of antibiotic therapy. PJP- prophylaxis with monthly inhaled pentamidin (300 mg) was initiated.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 78-year-old male with seronegative rheumatoid arthritis presented with a 2-week history of arthralgia, nausea, confusion, and exertional shortness of breath two months after adding tofacitinib to methotrexate and prednisolone.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed 6 months earlier with seronegative, non-erosive rheumatoid arthritis (>10 swollen/tender joints across wrists, hands, and feet with a 3-year history of arthralgia), the patient was initially treated with oral prednisone (20 mg/day) and subcutaneous methotrexate (15 mg/week). Two months prior to admission, due to inadequate efficacy of methotrexate monotherapy and dislike of injections, he was switched to oral tofacitinib (10 mg daily), oral methotrexate (20 mg weekly), and low-dose oral prednisolone (5 mg daily). He presented to the hospital with a 2-week history of worsening arthralgia, nausea, confusion, and exertional dyspnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Seronegative (RF-IgM negative, anti-CCP negative), non-erosive rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 6 months prior (3-year symptom history).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for arthralgia, nausea, confusion, and exertional dyspnea (no dyspnea at rest). Subsequent inpatient drug adverse reactions included severe hyponatremia/worsening confusion from IV TMP/SMX and severe thrombocytopenia from primaquine. Home medications were tofacitinib (10 mg PO daily), methotrexate (20 mg PO weekly), and prednisolone (5 mg PO daily).

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: Auricular temperature 36.5 °C, blood pressure 178/95 mmHg, heart rate 75 beats/min, and room-air SpO2 88%–90% at rest dropping to 80% on exertion. Musculoskeletal and cardiopulmonary exam: Bilateral symmetrical swelling and tenderness of the wrists and ankles; normal heart and lung auscultation without signs of venous congestion.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission endocrine and metabolic labs: Severe PTH-independent calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia with albumin-corrected serum calcium 3.12 mmol/L (normal: 2.0–2.6 mmol/L), elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D at 162 ng/L (normal: 22–111 ng/L), and appropriately suppressed intact PTH <0.5 pmol/L (normal <1.3 pmol/L). Inpatient adverse drug reaction labs: Day 10 severe hyponatremia on TMP/SMX (sodium dropped from 136 to 119 mmol/L, normal: 136–144 mmol/L); day 14 severe thrombocytopenia on primaquine/clindamycin (platelets dropped from 441 G/L to 83 G/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Whole-body CT scan: Bilateral interstitial pneumonic infiltrates without pleural effusions or malignancy. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) molecular testing: Positive PCR for Pneumocystis jirovecii and Rhinovirus A/B/C.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP; confirmed by positive BAL PCR and bilateral interstitial infiltrates on CT, with Rhinovirus A/B/C co-colonization) presenting with calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia (corrected calcium 3.12 mmol/L, 1,25-(OH)2D 162 ng/L) in a rheumatoid arthritis patient receiving triple immunosuppression (tofacitinib, methotrexate, and prednisolone). Plan and clinical course: Managed in the ICU with noninvasive ventilation / high-flow oxygen, intravenous TMP/SMX (15 mg/kg/day), and oral prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day). On day 10, severe hyponatremia (119 mmol/L) and worsening encephalopathy prompted switching from TMP/SMX to second-line clindamycin plus primaquine, which was stopped 4 days later due to primaquine-induced thrombocytopenia (platelets 83 G/L). After 17 days of antimicrobial therapy, both his respiratory failure and hypercalcemia resolved, and he was transitioned to secondary PJP prophylaxis with monthly inhaled pentamidine (300 mg).
